findings.where: Screen 9 (Section A (c)), Given box, EV charging line
findings.what: "Taken as four single-phase outlets" carries no practice-value label, although the case file marks it as one (p.ev.outlet): the drawing does not say whether the 2 x 32 A outlets are single-phase or three-phase, and three-phase outlets would put 128 A on every phase instead of 42.67 A. Add "(a practice value: the drawing does not say whether the outlets are single- or three-phase)".

findings.where: Screen 3 (The why): the rule box, the say line and the step's read sentence
findings.what: The 0.30 A neutral for the course's split is given with no word on harmonics, yet every fitting on DBL2 is fluorescent or LED, and their third-harmonic currents add in the neutral (slides p.33 to 37; the lesson's own 'ignores' and the fact-check say so, and only the Keep card says 'no harmonics'). Add one line under the rule: fundamental currents only; these fittings also draw third harmonics, which add in the neutral (lesson 4).

"Motors: 100% of the largest" cuts the row short. Its source [^19] gives '100% f.l. of largest motor +80% f.l. of second largest motor +60% f.l. of remaining motors', so on a job with two motors this list would leave the others out. Give the whole row, or write '100% of the largest (the showroom has only one)'.

The EV trap's citation starts with 'BS 7671 722.311.201 (NAPIT)', but that regulation (Amendment 1) lets load curtailment count and does not forbid diversity (research source 172; the fact-check flagged it as a note). Put the IEC wording in the Schneider guide first, and name 722.311.201 as the regulation that allows load curtailment.

Each revealed line pops in. 'enter' is added to the line's

, but the CSS rule is '.wl .w.enter', which needs class 'w' on that same element, and only the inner span has it. Change the selector, and its k-testing and reduced-motion copies, to '.wl p.enter'.

findings.where: Screen 3, the four bars (film s2 at 0.00 s)
findings.what: From the first frame the value labels already show the final 24.35 A while the bars are still growing from zero. On each card move the values jump at once while the bars ease over 0.5 s. Print the eased value from shownBars() so the numbers and the bars agree.

findings.where: Screen 9 (Section A (c)), Given box, after 'Skip to the practice'
findings.what: The sockets 'as standard circuits' and the fixed points 'as heating and power' are named, but their percentages (100% + 50%, 100% + 75%) appear only on screen 5, which the skip passes. 'Lighting, at 100% (step 5)' also points to a screen he did not see. Repeat the two allowances in the Given box so the part stands alone, as a C&G question would.
DBL1's six IP65 2D bulkheads are worked with the LEDs (at 0.95, with no ballast allowance), and the screen never says so. Screen 8 now says this for the bollards; add the same few words here.

findings.where: Screen 9, the line after a right answer
findings.what: 'A real split leaves one phase a little heavier' understates it. Four 32 A EV outlets cannot share evenly over three phases, so one phase carries 64 A of EV against the 42.67 A even share unless other circuits move off it. Say why the real figure is higher.

findings.where: Screen 8 (Section A (b)), the working revealed after two misses
findings.what: After two misses, nothing says that part (c) carries the course's 8.22 A forward. Part (a) has this missNote ('Part (b) carries the course's 4594 W'); add the same here.

findings.where: Screens 7 to 9, the label 'Section A · Question 3'
findings.what: His assignment's question 3 is the DBL2 submain design (lesson 8), and this part answers pack questions 1b and 10, so the course's own numbering can be mixed up with the pack's. Label it as the course's question, or tie it to pack question 10.

findings.where: Screen 1 (Do you still have it?), the options
findings.what: The two wrong options carry absolute words ('every design', 'always 66%') that give the right one away, so 'Still there' proves little to a Level 4 holder. A slip phrased without an absolute (for example 'Yes, wherever the On-Site Guide gives a percentage') would test the idea.

Point 4 cites Whitfield 6.2.1's definition of maximum demand. That supports what maximum demand is, not a reason a designer applies diversity. Re-point it, or cite slides p.10's 'design a circuit using common sense rather than its maximum demand'.

findings.where: Screen 3 at 360 px, the 'Heaviest phase' readout
findings.what: It wraps to two lines ('L1 ·' above '24.35 A') while 'Neutral' beside it sits on one. Putting the phase in the label, or writing 'L1: 24.35 A' in a smaller weight, would keep the pair level.
'0 A' has no decimals, while '24.00 A' and '6.00 A' sit beside it (case figure l2.check.slip2 text). Print '0.00 A' to match.

findings.where: Screen 2, the red 'If it is skipped or wrong' note
findings.what: Both halves are cited to slides p.10, but p.10 supports only the 'too high' half (smaller cables, lower costs). The 'too low' half is the course's own words, and it could name the real consequence: the supply fuse or the submain's device and cable carry more than they were chosen for.
